function.name: search_class
function.description:
Search for a class in the codebase.

Only the signature of the class is returned. The class signature
includes class name, base classes, and signatures for all of its methods/properties.

Args:
    class_name (string): Name of the class to search for.

function.name: search_class_in_file
function.description:
Search for a class in a given file.

Returns the actual code of the entire class definition.

Args:
    class_name (string): Name of the class to search for.
    file_name (string): The file to search in. Must be a valid python file name.

function.name: search_method_in_file
function.description:
Search for a method in a given file.

Returns the actual code of the method.

Args:
    method_name (string): Name of the method to search for.
    file_name (string): The file to search in. Must be a valid python file name.

function.name: search_method_in_class
function.description:
Search for a method in a given class.

Returns the actual code of the method.

Args:
    method_name (string): Name of the method to search for.
    class_name (string): Consider only methods in this class.

function.name: search_method
function.description:
Search for a method in the entire codebase.

Returns the actual code of the method.

Args:
    method_name (string): Name of the method to search for.

function.name: search_code
function.description:
Search for a code snippet in the entire codebase.

Returns the method that contains the code snippet, if it is found inside a method.
Otherwise, returns the region of code surrounding it.

Args:
    code_str (string): The code snippet to search for.

function.name: search_code_in_file
function.description:
Search for a code snippet in a given file file.

Returns the entire method that contains the code snippet.

Args:
    code_str (string): The code snippet to search for.
    file_name (string): The file to search in. Must be a valid python file name in the project.

function.name: get_code_around_line
function.description:
Get the region of code around line `line_no` in the file `file_name`.

Args:
    file_name (str): The file name.
    line_no_str (str): The line number. (1-based)
    window_size_str (str): The number of lines before and after the line number.

function.name: readCode
function.description:
Read code with AST parsing and fuzzy search. Language auto-detected from file extension.
BEHAVIOR: • Small files (<10K chars): Returns FULL content • Large files (≥10K chars): Returns signatures (function/class names & line numbers)
MOST EFFICIENT USAGE: readCode <path>  # ALWAYS START WITH THIS - gets full content OR signatures If you get signatures and need specific code: 1. readCode <path> --selector <name>     # Read specific function/class 2. readCode <path> --line-start 10 --line-end 50  # Read specific line range
CRITICAL RULES: • NEVER use empty path '' - always specify a file or directory • ALWAYS call readCode <path> first - it auto-adapts to file size • Read each file ONCE - never repeat with different parameters • Use --selector or --line-start/end ONLY if first call returns signatures • Selector is just the name: "is_fits" NOT "def is_fits" • If you need directory listing, use safeBash 'ls -la <path>' or safeBash 'find <path> -name "*.py"'
EXAMPLES: readCode small.py                              # Returns: full content readCode large_file.py                         # Returns: signatures only readCode large_file.py --selector is_fits      # Returns: specific function readCode config.yaml --line-start 1 --line-end 50  # Returns: specific lines

path.description: File or directory path (REQUIRED - never use empty string '')

line_start.description: Start line number (1-indexed). Use with line_end for line-based reading.

line_end.description: End line number (1-indexed). Use with line_start for line-based reading.

function.name: editCode
function.description:
AST-based code editor. Auto-detects language, handles indentation.
PREFER str_replace FOR: • Single-line changes or small edits (< 5 lines) • Modifying a return statement, condition, or variable • Adding/removing a single statement within a function • Any change that doesn't require replacing the entire function
USE editCode ONLY FOR: • Adding NEW functions or methods (insert_node) • Deleting entire functions/classes (delete_node) • Complete function rewrites where >30% of lines change
CRITICAL - AVOID THESE MISTAKES: • Do NOT include import statements in replacement - they already exist • Do NOT use replace_node for small changes - use str_replace instead • Do NOT rewrite entire functions to change 1-2 lines
Operations: replace_node, insert_node, delete_node Possible Selectors: "ClassName", "functionName", "ClassName.methodName", "start", "end"
Examples: • editCode main.py insert_node Calculator --replacement "def add(self, a, b):\n    return a + b" • editCode main.py delete_node oldFunc • For small edits, use: str_replace file.py "old_line" "new_line"

operation.description: AST operation type: replace_node, insert_node, delete_node

function.name: str_replace
function.description:
Replace a unique string in a file. Safe tool that never crashes.
WHEN TO USE: • Use str_replace ONLY for very small edits (single line changes, simple text replacements) • For most code modifications, use editCode tool instead • For any function/class modifications, prefer editCode tool
IMPORTANT: - old_str must appear EXACTLY ONCE in the file - Automatically converts relative paths to absolute - Returns error message instead of crashing on failure
Usage: - str_replace /path/to/file.py "old text" "new text" - str_replace /path/to/file.py "text to delete" ""
The tool will: 1. Check if file exists 2. Verify old_str appears exactly once 3. Perform replacement 4. Save file
Returns success message or error (never crashes shell).

old_str.description: Exact string to replace (must be unique in file)

new_str.description: Replacement string (default: empty string to delete)

function.name: create_file
function.description:
Create a new file with content. Safe tool that never crashes.
IMPORTANT: - Use this instead of bash heredoc or inline python to avoid shell crashes - Perfect for creating reproduction scripts that might error - Automatically creates parent directories - Overwrites existing files by default
Usage: - create_file reproduce_bug.py "from module import func\nfunc()" - create_file test.txt "hello world"
The tool will: 1. Create parent directories if needed 2. Write content to file (overwrites if exists) 3. Return success/error (never crashes shell)
WHY USE THIS: When creating reproduction scripts that might crash (e.g., testing bugs), use create_file instead of inline python execution. This prevents the error from crashing your shell session.
Example workflow: 1. create_file reproduce_bug.py "code that might crash" 2. python reproduce_bug.py  # Error contained in subprocess 3. Fix the bug 4. python reproduce_bug.py  # Verify fix

file_path.description: Path to file to create (absolute or relative)

content.description: File content (use quotes for multi-line, default empty)

function.name: view_diff
function.description: Inspect the current patch. Optional paths selects files with native git pathspecs; omit for all changes.

function.name: submit
function.description: Submit the current patch and finish. Optional paths selects the intended source files with native git pathspecs; omit for all changes.

function.name: run_tests
function.description: Run the repository test runner: pytest, or Django runtests.py. Supply paths/labels and runner options in targets; an empty array runs its default selection. New or modified tests are allowed.
